body.statement:
Let \(P\) be a conditional-mean interior observed law induced by a full-data law in the global OVS model \(\mathcal M\).  Under global retained-cell overlap and the fourth-moment condition,
\[
\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp
=\overline{\{a(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O):a\text{ measurable and }
E_P[(a(X)'Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}(O))^2]<\infty\}}^{L_2(P)}.
\]
With the objects in Definition \(\ref{def:ovs-normal-projection}\),
\[
\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}
=\psi_P^0-r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)^\dagger
Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}
\tag{15}
\]
is the canonical gradient of \(\tau_\omega\) in the published class, including singular and redundant fixed-law cases, and
\[
V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
=E_P[(\psi_P^0)^2]
-E_P[r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)^\dagger r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)].
\tag{16}
\]
The former complete-normal gradient \(\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}\) is the canonical gradient only in the larger localized observed model \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{loc}}\).  It remains a valid gradient in the published subclass, but
\[
V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\le V_{\mathrm{can}},
\qquad
V_{\mathrm{can}}-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
=E_P[(\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}-\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P})^2],
\tag{17}
\]
with equality if and only if
\[
E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}\mid X]=0
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\tag{18}
\]

The conditional loading \(b^\star\) remains the singular-safe optimum inside the aggregate pairwise-score family.  In particular,
\[
V_{\mathrm{agg}}
=\operatorname{Var}_P\{\omega'h(X)\}
+E_P[b^\star(X)'\Gamma_P(X)b^\star(X)],
\tag{19}
\]
and every measurable feasible \(b\), with \(A'b(X)=\omega\) almost surely and \(b(X)'\Psi_P\in L_2(P)\), satisfies
\[
\operatorname{Var}_P\{b(X)'\Psi_P\}-V_{\mathrm{agg}}
=E_P[(b(X)-b^\star(X))'\Gamma_P(X)(b(X)-b^\star(X))]\ge0.
\tag{20}
\]
The three nested frontiers obey
\[
V_{\mathrm{agg}}-V_{\mathrm{OVS}}
=E_P[(\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}-\phi_{\mathrm{can},P})^2]
+E_P[(\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}-\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P})^2].
\tag{21}
\]
Thus \(b^\star(X)'\Psi_P\) reaches the localized bound exactly when
\(E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}\mid X]=0\), and it reaches the published OVS bound exactly when
\[
E_P[Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}\mid X]=0
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\tag{22}
\]
In particular, score-family projection is not called semiparametric efficiency unless (22) is verified.
body.justification: The theorem proves the exhaustive published-class Moore--Penrose projection and the nested inequalities \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\le V_{\mathrm{can}}\le V_{\mathrm{agg}}\).
body.gap: Neither conditional nor constant optimization over terminal pairwise scores is semiparametric efficiency unless its full OVS normal equation holds.
body.consumer: The result supplies separate aggregate, local-model, and published-class efficiency diagnostics.
body.proof_tex:
The tangent-normal identity in the first display is equation (2) of Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\).  The reference-score-gradient lemma gives, for every \(s\in\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}\),
\[
\dot\tau_{\omega,P}[s]=E_P[\psi_P^0s].
\tag{23}
\]
We calculate the orthogonal projection of \(\psi_P^0\) onto the normal space without assuming invertibility.  Abbreviate \(Z=Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\), \(K=K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\), and \(r=r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\).  Conditional on \(X=x\), \(K(x)\) is symmetric positive semidefinite.  If \(v\in\ker K(x)\), then
\[
0=v'K(x)v=E_P[(v'Z)^2\mid X=x],
\]
so \(v'Z=0\) conditionally almost surely and
\[
v'r(x)=E_P[v'Z\psi_P^0\mid X=x]=0.
\]
Therefore
\[
r(x)\in\{\ker K(x)\}^\perp=\operatorname{range}K(x),
\qquad K(x)K(x)^\dagger r(x)=r(x).
\tag{24}
\]
The Moore--Penrose map is Borel measurable because, for a symmetric positive semidefinite matrix,
\[
K^\dagger=\lim_{j\to\infty}(K^2+j^{-1}I)^{-1}K.
\tag{25}
\]

Put \(p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=r'K^\dagger Z\).  Symmetry, (24), and the Moore--Penrose identities give
\[
E_P[p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}^2\mid X]
=r'K^\dagger KK^\dagger r
=r'K^\dagger r
=E_P[\psi_P^0p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\mid X].
\tag{26}
\]
Consequently \(p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\in L_2(P)\).  For every measurable \(a\) for which \(a(X)'Z\in L_2(P)\),
\[
E_P[(\psi_P^0-p_{\mathrm{OVS},P})a(X)'Z]
=E_P[a(X)'\{r(X)-K(X)K(X)^\dagger r(X)\}]=0.
\tag{27}
\]
Equations (26)--(27) and tangent exhaustion prove
\[
p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp}\psi_P^0,
\qquad
\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}}\psi_P^0.
\tag{28}
\]
Combining (23) and (28) shows that \(\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\) represents the derivative and belongs to the tangent space; it is therefore the canonical gradient.  Taking expectations in (26) proves (16).  If two Moore--Penrose coefficient versions differ in \(\ker K(X)\), their products with \(Z\) agree almost surely, so singularity does not make the projected random variable ambiguous.

Apply the same calculation to the local normal vector \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\).  Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\) gives
\[
p_{\mathrm{per},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_P^\perp}\psi_P^0,
\qquad
\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_P}\psi_P^0.
\tag{29}
\]
Because \(\mathcal T_P^\perp\subseteq\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp\), nested orthogonal projections imply
\[
p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}-p_{\mathrm{per},P}
\in\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp\cap\mathcal T_P,
\qquad
\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}
=\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}+(p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}-p_{\mathrm{per},P}).
\tag{30}
\]
The terms on the right of (30) are orthogonal.  Pythagoras proves (17).  Also \(p_{\mathrm{per},P}\) belongs to the published normal space, so subtracting it from the ambient gradient preserves (23) on the published tangent: this proves validity of the local gradient in the subclass.  It is canonical there exactly when it belongs to \(\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}\), which, by equation (2) of the observable-equivalence theorem, is equivalent to (18).

We now establish the aggregate identities.  On the observable equality model, Definition \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) and the zero conditional means of all residual terms give
\[
E_P[\Psi_P\mid X]=Ah(X).
\tag{31}
\]
Thus every feasible loading has conditional mean \(\omega'h(X)\), and iterated variance gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}_P\{b(X)'\Psi_P\}
=\operatorname{Var}_P\{\omega'h(X)\}
+E_P[b(X)'\Gamma_P(X)b(X)].
\tag{32}
\]
By Lemma \(\ref{lem:singular-operator}\), \(A'b^\star=\omega\) and \(N'\Gamma b^\star=0\).  For \(d=b-b^\star\), feasibility gives \(A'd=0\), hence \(d=Nz\) for a measurable \(z\).  It follows that
\[
d'\Gamma b^\star=z'N'\Gamma b^\star=0.
\]
Expanding (32) proves (19)--(20), including uniqueness only modulo \(\ker\Gamma(X)\cap\ker A'\).

Let \(b^{\mathrm{ref}}\) place weight \(\omega_k\) on \((k,c_0(k))\) and zero on the other coordinates.  Then \(A'b^{\mathrm{ref}}=\omega\) and \(\psi_P^0=b^{\mathrm{ref}\prime}\Psi_P\).  Since \(b^{\mathrm{ref}}-b^\star\in\operatorname{col}N\), equation (14) of Theorem \(\ref{thm:observable-equivalence}\) yields
\[
p_{\mathrm{agg},P}:=\psi_P^0-\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}
=(b^{\mathrm{ref}}-b^\star(X))'R_P\in\mathcal C_P.
\tag{33}
\]
Moreover, (31), \(N'A=0\), and \(N'\Gamma b^\star=0\) imply
\[
E_P[N'R_P\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}\mid X]
=N'\{\Gamma_P+Ahh'A'\}b^\star=0.
\tag{34}
\]
Therefore \(p_{\mathrm{agg},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\psi_P^0\).

The nested normal spaces are
\[
\mathcal C_P\subseteq\mathcal T_P^\perp
\subseteq\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}^\perp.
\]
Successive projection increments are orthogonal, so
\[
\phi_{\mathrm{agg},P}
=\phi_{\mathrm{can},P}+(p_{\mathrm{per},P}-p_{\mathrm{agg},P})
=\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}
+(p_{\mathrm{OVS},P}-p_{\mathrm{per},P})
+(p_{\mathrm{per},P}-p_{\mathrm{agg},P}).
\]
Pythagoras proves (21).  Finally, orthogonality to every measurable multiple of a finite normal vector is equivalent, by conditional expectation, to its conditional cross-moment with that vector being zero.  Applying this first to \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\) and then to \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) proves the two equality characterizations, including (22).
